script: James Harden just became the fourth player in NBA history to enter the 500 million dollar club. The other players in the club are LeBron James, Kevin Durant, and Steph Curry. All four players are MVPs. But Harden is the only one so far without a ring or Finals MVP. Another interesting aspect to this is how he entered the $500 million club. He did this through his recent signing with the Cleveland Cavaliers. Harden just landed a 3-year, $97 million fully guaranteed contract to return to the Cavs. That deal includes a third-year player option and a 15% trade kicker. Harden turns 37 on August 26th, so the Cavs are ready to give about $100 million to a 37-40 year old Harden. The Cavs also became Harden's second-highest earning team, who paid him $136.2 million, behind the Rockets in first place who paid him $173.5 million. The Cavs were hoping to land James the summer, but they did to keep James. James Harden, not LeBron James. Which is why they ended up recently trading for Peyton Watson, who just came off of a 14 point per game season and is a young 6'8" athletic upward-forward. A lot of teams in the East are playing with a chip on their shoulder this season with much to prove and to silence doubters. Let's see if the Cavs have made a good choice with Harden, or if they should have pushed harder for LeBron by trading one of their starters.
